name: UPSTREAM
aliases: Urodynamics for Prostate Surgery Trial: Randomised Evaluation of Assessment Methods
question: Does adding invasive urodynamics to routine noninvasive tests before treatment decisions for bothersome male LUTS leave symptoms no worse and reduce surgery?

design.blinding: open-label; men and hospital staff unblinded; co-applicants blinded to arm throughout recruitment and analysis, junior statistician unblinded for monitoring-committee reporting

arms.label: Routine noninvasive tests plus invasive urodynamics

design.population: 820 men (median age 68) at 26 English NHS hospitals who had received conservative or medical therapy and sought further treatment, possibly including surgery, for bothersome LUTS; catheter dependence, relevant neurologic disease, prostate or bladder cancer treatment, prior prostate surgery and unfitness for surgery were excluded.
design.description: Pragmatic multicenter open-label noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: Eur Urol accepted manuscript PDF pp4, 6-9 and Tables PDF p2 (Table 1); CONSORT PDF p2; HTA 2020 PDF pp37, 39, 42, 50

verdictNote: IPSS noninferior at 18 months, but urodynamics did not reduce the surgery rate.
takeaway: Adding invasive urodynamics to routine noninvasive tests in men with bothersome LUTS considering prostate surgery gave an 18-month IPSS noninferior to routine tests alone (adjusted difference −0.33, 95% CI −1.47 to 0.80; margin 1 point) and did not reduce surgery (38% versus 36%).

reports.label: 18-month primary report
reports.citation: Drake MJ, Lewis AL, Young GJ, et al. "Diagnostic Assessment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Men Considering Prostate Surgery: A Noninferiority Randomised Controlled Trial of Urodynamics in 26 Hospitals." *Eur Urol.* 2020;78(5):701-710. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2020.06.004

results.measure: Mean IPSS at 18 months (0–35); adjusted difference, urodynamics minus routine care
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF pp8-9; Tables PDF p2, Table 2
results.note: Noninferiority margin 1 point, declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI was below 1 point; intention-to-treat linear regression adjusted for centre and baseline IPSS. 340 versus 329 men had an 18-month IPSS and 328 versus 313 entered the adjusted analysis (12 and 16 lacked a baseline IPSS). The IPSS fell from 18.5 (n = 403) to 12.6 with urodynamics and from 19.4 (n = 371) to 13.1 with routine care.

results.measure: Mean IPSS at 18 months, per-protocol; adjusted difference
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p9; Tables PDF p2, Table 2
results.note: Men who did not receive their allocated pathway were excluded; the upper limit of 1.05 is slightly above the 1-point margin.

results.measure: Complier average causal effect on 18-month IPSS (instrumental-variable regression using allocation); adjusted difference
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p9; Tables PDF p2, Table 2
results.note: 330 versus 339 men in the as-treated groups; the authors describe the result as generally similar to the intention-to-treat analysis.

results.measure: IPSS quality-of-life item at 18 months (0–6); adjusted difference, urodynamics minus routine care
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p10; Tables PDF p3, Table 4
results.note: Baseline 4.1 versus 4.2; the interval excludes the 0.5-point minimal clinically important difference.

results.measure: Tests of interaction between arm and prespecified subgroups (including age and urinary function) on 18-month IPSS
results.note: No evident interactions; the authors call the tests underpowered.

results.measure: Urological surgery within 18 months
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p10; Tables PDF p3, Table 3
results.note: The key secondary hypothesis was that urodynamics would reduce surgery, and the reduction was not shown; adjusted for centre, denominators are men with surgery outcome known.

results.measure: Surgery recommended by the surgeon after assessment
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p10; Tables PDF p3, Table 3
results.note: Adjusted for centre. A post hoc internal validation of the recommendations against flow and urodynamic data gave 65% recommended in both as-treated arms (supplement).

results.measure: Median time from randomisation to surgery
results.note: Interquartile range 141-327 days with urodynamics and 106-284 days with routine care. In both arms at least 75% of men had TURP, the rest laser surgery, bladder neck incision, UroLift or another procedure.

results.measure: Mean maximum flow rate at 18 months (mL/s); adjusted difference
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p10; Tables PDF p3, Table 3
results.note: 18 men lacked baseline data; adjusted for baseline Qmax and centre.

results.measure: Mean maximum flow rate about 4 months after surgery (mL/s) in men who had surgery; adjusted difference
results.note: One man excluded for missing baseline data.

results.measure: ICIQ-MLUTS voiding scale at 18 months; adjusted difference
ICIQ-MLUTS incontinence scale at 18 months; adjusted difference
Nocturia more than once per night at 18 months (ICIQ-MLUTS)
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p10; Tables PDF p3, Table 4
results.note: The authors say it may be a chance finding given the number of secondary comparisons.

results.measure: Reduced or absent ejaculation at 18 months (ICIQ-MLUTSsex)
results.note: The authors report sexual symptoms as similar between arms and at baseline levels.

results.measure: Post hoc interaction between arm and surgery on change in IPSS
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p10 (Figure 2, Supplementary Table 4)
results.note: The authors report surgery as potentially more beneficial in the routine care arm and offer delayed surgery in the urodynamics arm as one explanation. The HTA report gives p = 0.006 for the interaction between surgery and arm.

harms.label: Adverse events (all events)
harms.note: 428 events in total. No evidence that one arm was superior for adverse events per participant; related serious events were similar at event level. The slight excess in the urodynamics arm came largely from events attributed to urodynamics, for example urinary tract infection.

harms.label: Deaths within 18 months
harms.note: An independent reviewer judged none related to diagnostic testing or treatment.

delivery.label: Randomized
delivery.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF pp3, 9; CONSORT PDF p2
delivery.note: 820 men randomized 1:1 between 1 October 2014 and 31 December 2016 from 8,671 assessed; 5,910 were not eligible, 662 declined and 1,279 were not included for an unidentified reason.

delivery.label: Urodynamics received
delivery.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p9; CONSORT PDF p2
delivery.note: Men allocated to urodynamics who did not have it: 14 declined, 14 had resolved symptoms, 10 cancelled or did not attend, 10 had an unsuccessful attempt, 3 had surgery arranged first, 17 reason missing, 6 withdrew. Routine care men who did not receive routine care only: 22 by clinician decision to use urodynamics, 2 at patient request, 2 from staff error in conducting urodynamics, 2 reason missing, 5 withdrew.

delivery.label: Withdrawals
delivery.note: 67 withdrawals, most often for poor health. The adjusted 18-month IPSS analysis included 641 men (78%): 328 (77%) with urodynamics and 313 (80%) with routine care.

delivery.label: Routine care crossovers to urodynamics
delivery.value: Mean 18-month IPSS 17.3 (n = 24) in routine care men who had urodynamics versus 12.8 (n = 305) in routine care compliers; baseline 22.6 versus 19.2.
delivery.note: The authors treat this as a small sample and note the difference was present at baseline.

delivery.label: Urodynamic quality control
delivery.value: A quality-control review found errors of standardisation, testing, interpretation and equipment maintenance, most with low risk to decisions; erroneous diagnosis of bladder outlet obstruction in 5.5% of tests.
delivery.note: Reported separately by Aiello et al., Neurourol Urodyn 2020.

delivery.label: Surgery rates below plan
delivery.value: Overall surgery rates were lower than anticipated; the design used rates from audit of local practice and surgical trials.
delivery.note: The authors attribute the lower rates to trends toward fewer surgical recommendations and acceptances during the trial and see no signal of a difference in surgery rates to suggest an underpowered study.

reports.label: Full HTA report
reports.citation: Lewis AL, Young GJ, Selman LE, et al. "Urodynamics tests for the diagnosis and management of bladder outlet obstruction in men: the UPSTREAM non-inferiority RCT." *Health Technol Assess.* 2020;24(42):1-122. doi:10.3310/hta24420
reports.followUp: 18 months after randomisation (IPSS at 6, 12 and 18 months)

results.measure: IPSS quality-of-life score at 18 months (0–6); adjusted difference, urodynamics minus routine care
results.note: 340 versus 329 men had an 18-month IPSS; 343 versus 332 had the quality-of-life item.

results.measure: Mean IPSS at 18 months after multiple imputation; adjusted difference
results.note: 427 versus 393 men; the upper limit is just inside the margin.

results.note: Adjusted for centre.

Surgery within 18 months in men for whom surgery was or was not recommended
Median time from randomisation to surgery
results.note: 291 men had surgery for LUTS in the trial.

results.note: Effect shown is the interaction between surgery and trial arm on 18-month IPSS (Table 13); it fell to 1.14 (95% CI −0.94 to 3.22; p = 0.283) when analysed as treated, which the report suggests may be a chance finding.

results.measure: Mean maximum flow rate at 18 months (mL/s); adjusted difference
results.note: 268 versus 270 men; baseline 11.85 versus 12.39 mL/s.

results.measure: Nocturia more than once per night at 18 months (ICIQ-MLUTS)
results.note: One of many secondary comparisons; the report says it may be a chance finding.

harms.label: Adverse events
harms.note: 32% of men in the urodynamics arm and 30% in the routine care arm had at least one event; 43–44% of events were related to testing or treatment in both arms.

harms.label: Serious adverse events due to urodynamics
harms.locator: PDF p64, Table 15; intention to treat
harms.note: Expected non-serious events due to urodynamics numbered 10 versus 1 and unexpected non-serious events 3 versus 0.

harms.label: Serious adverse events due to surgery
harms.locator: PDF p64, Table 15; intention to treat

harms.label: Clavien–Dindo grade IIIa and IIIb surgery-related events
harms.locator: PDF p64, Table 15; intention to treat
harms.note: Events graded III without a subdivision numbered 4 versus 5; no grade IV or V events.

harms.label: Acute urinary retention episodes
harms.locator: PDF p64, Table 15; intention to treat
harms.note: Counted as adverse events; the report says there appeared to be more in the routine care arm and carried out no formal test.

harms.label: Deaths within 18 months
harms.note: p = 0.047; the report found none related to trial procedures.

delivery.label: Received the allocated pathway
delivery.note: p < 0.001. In the urodynamics arm 68 men did not have the test (14 declined, 14 reported resolved symptoms, 10 cancelled or did not attend, 3 had surgery arranged first, 10 had an unsuccessful attempt); 28 routine care men had urodynamics, 22 by clinician decision (PDF p50).

delivery.label: Operations in men with an 18-month IPSS who had LUTS surgery

values.exp: TURP 102, laser 19, bladder neck incision 5, UroLift 10 (of 137)
values.ctl: TURP 99, laser 5, bladder neck incision 4, UroLift 7 (of 116)

delivery.note: The trial did not specify operations.

delivery.label: Urodynamic quality control
delivery.value: At least 10% of traces from each centre were reviewed against ICS standards; most practice was broadly compliant, with some non-compliant incidents.

delivery.label: Satisfaction with urodynamics
delivery.value: Median overall satisfaction 10/10; 294/303 (97%) would take the test again; 77/302 (26%) found it worse than expected.
delivery.note: Among 353 men in the urodynamics arm who had the test.

delivery.label: Planned sample size and observed surgery rate
delivery.value: 310 men per arm (SD 5, one-sided alpha 5%, 80% power), inflated to 388 per arm; surgery was planned around 73% versus 60%, observed 36–38%.

reports.label: Exploratory predictors of surgery and outcome
reports.citation: Young GJ, Metcalfe C, Lane JA, et al. "Prostate Surgery for Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: Do We Need Urodynamics to Find the Right Candidates? Exploratory Findings from the UPSTREAM Trial." *Eur Urol Focus.* 2022;8(5):1331-1339. doi:10.1016/j.euf.2021.11.010

results.measure: Surgery recommended after a BOOI of 40 or more versus below 40 (men who had urodynamics)
results.note: Analysis by pathway received, not allocation.

results.measure: Area under the ROC curve of the best routine-care model, and of the urodynamics model without and with BOOI
results.note: The routine-care model used Qmax, age, ICIQ voiding subscale and IPSS quality of life; BCI added nothing.

results.measure: Mean change in IPSS at 18 months
results.note: Pathway received; men with baseline IPSS of 7 or less were excluded from these analyses.

results.measure: Baseline values associated with an IPSS fall of 3 or more points after surgery
results.note: IPSS above 16, age below 74 years, Qmax below 9.8 mL/s, ICIQ voiding subscale above 8, and, in men who had urodynamics, BOOI above 47.6 or BCI above 123.0.

delivery.label: Subgroup in which urodynamic indices predicted outcome better
delivery.value: Qmax above 15 mL/s (n = 16); the relationship between BOOI or BCI and IPSS change was weaker when detrusor overactivity was present.
delivery.note: The authors describe the analyses as exploratory signposts based on small groups.

reports.label: 5-year follow-up
reports.citation: Clout M, Lewis AL, Cochrane M, et al. "Five-year Follow-up of the Urodynamics for Prostate Surgery Trial; Randomised Evaluation of Assessment Methods-A Noninferiority Randomised Controlled Trial of Urodynamics." *Eur Urol Focus.* 2025;11(4):618-624. doi:10.1016/j.euf.2025.02.004
reports.followUp: 5 years after randomisation (questionnaires October 2019 to December 2021)

results.measure: IPSS at 5 years; adjusted difference, urodynamics minus routine care
results.locator: PDF p5, Table 1; PDF pp4-5, Section 3.2
results.note: The 1-point margin from 18 months was retained. The upper limit of 1.93 exceeds it, and the authors state that noninferiority could not be confirmed because of the wide interval; the point estimate favored urodynamics at 18 months (-0.33) and routine care at 5 years. 208 versus 202 men had a 5-year IPSS; 4 and 3 lacked a baseline IPSS. Adjusted for centre and baseline IPSS.

results.measure: Surgery for LUTS within 5 years from NHS England routine data; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: The hypothesised reduction in surgery did not emerge. Logistic regression adjusted for centre; 415 versus 386 men had routine data.

results.measure: IPSS quality-of-life score at 5 years (0-6); adjusted difference
results.note: 211 versus 204 men; 2 and 1 lacked a baseline quality-of-life score.

results.measure: Median time from randomisation to first LUTS procedure in routine data
results.note: 242 days overall (interquartile range 131-435; range 8 to 1,812). Intervention 260 days (149-417) and routine care 232 days (112-437).

results.measure: ICIQ-MLUTS voiding scale at 5 years (0-20); adjusted difference
ICIQ-MLUTS incontinence scale at 5 years (0-24); adjusted difference
Nocturia more than once per night at 5 years (ICIQ-MLUTS)
results.locator: PDF p6, Table 2; PDF p7, Section 4
results.note: The 18-month difference in favor of urodynamics (59% versus 67%) did not persist as a significant difference; the authors note nocturia has a complex pathophysiology.

results.measure: Reduced or absent ejaculation at 5 years (ICIQ-MLUTSsex)
Painful ejaculation at 5 years (ICIQ-MLUTSsex)
results.locator: PDF p6, Table 2; PDF p7, Section 4
results.note: The only sexual item that differed; the authors find no clear mechanistic explanation. Logistic regression not adjusted for centre.

harms.label: Deaths by 5 years (ONS records)
harms.locator: PDF p6, Section 3.5.2; PDF p7, Section 4
harms.note: Median time to death 35 months with urodynamics and 40 months with routine care; the authors describe no difference between groups.

delivery.label: Completed 5-year questionnaires
delivery.note: Of 570 men contactable, 415 returned at least a partly completed questionnaire (72.8%) and 329 completed all time points (170 and 159). Questionnaires were sent October 2019 to December 2021, with a £20 voucher for return and up to three contact attempts. Non-completers had more comorbidities (71% versus 64%); completion was affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

delivery.label: Routine NHS data obtained
delivery.note: Details of 802 men (98%) were sent to NHS England, which failed to trace one; the linked data were received in 2023 and filtered by treatment specialty with a code list derived by two clinicians.

delivery.label: Men with a LUTS procedure in routine data
delivery.value: 347 men, 180 with urodynamics and 167 with routine care; the most common code was M653 (185 procedures).
delivery.locator: PDF pp5-6, Section 3.5.1; PDF p6, Section 4
delivery.note: The 347 include the 291 reported at 18 months. The authors report 43% at 5 years against 37% at 18 months.

delivery.label: Surgery rates below plan
delivery.value: The protocol assumed surgery in 73% of routine care and 60% of urodynamics men; observed rates stayed lower at 5 years.
delivery.note: The authors read this as a shift away from surgery for male LUTS.

reports.label: 5-year HTA report and costs
reports.dateLocator: HTA 2025 title page: published July 2025, Vol. 29, Issue 26; exact day not given
reports.citation: Clout M, Lewis AL, Cochrane M, et al. "Urodynamics tests for the diagnosis and management of male bladder outlet obstruction: long-term follow-up of the UPSTREAM non-inferiority RCT." *Health Technol Assess.* 2025;29(26). doi:10.3310/slpt4675
reports.followUp: 5 years after randomisation (data from 4 to 6 years accepted)

results.measure: IPSS at 5 years; adjusted difference, urodynamics minus routine care
results.locator: HTA 2025 pp18-19, Table 6; scientific summary pxiii
results.note: The 1-point margin was retained; noninferiority could not be confirmed given the wide interval, which the report attributes to the smaller sample, and it calls the study underpowered to confirm noninferiority. 208 versus 202 men; 4 and 3 lacked a baseline IPSS.

results.measure: 18-month IPSS in the men who also had a 5-year IPSS; adjusted difference
results.note: 202 versus 196 men; the report says this resembles the Phase I result, so the shift in point estimate between 18 months and 5 years is not an artifact of who responded.

results.measure: 5-year IPSS, per-protocol by urodynamics status recorded in Phase I; adjusted difference
results.note: 189 versus 190 men. Every 5-year sensitivity analysis in Table 13 has an upper limit above 1 point (per-protocol by routine-data status 0.63, 95% CI -1.27 to 2.53; multiple imputation 0.75, 95% CI -0.58 to 2.08; adjustment for time since surgery 0.54, 95% CI -0.92 to 2.00).

results.measure: Surgery for LUTS within 5 years from routine data; adjusted odds ratio
results.note: Logistic regression adjusted for centre; 415 versus 386 men with routine data.

results.measure: Men having first LUTS surgery in each 6-month period after randomisation
results.note: Percentages are of the 180 and 167 men with surgery. Later 6-month periods from 18 to 60 months: 11, 4, 5, 7, 2, 3, 2 men with urodynamics and 9, 8, 2, 4, 5, 3, 1 with routine care.

results.measure: Mean IPSS at baseline and 5 years in men who had LUTS surgery (routine data)
results.note: Men without surgery: 17.01 to 15.33 (n = 105) with urodynamics and 17.09 to 15.65 (n = 106) with routine care. Not a prespecified analysis.

results.measure: Interaction between surgery and arm on 5-year IPSS; adjusted difference in surgery effect, urodynamics minus routine care
results.note: Surgery lowered the IPSS in both arms (-3.25 with urodynamics, 95% CI -5.35 to -1.14; -6.30 with routine care, 95% CI -8.57 to -4.03). The report calls the analysis hypothesis-generating.

results.measure: Interaction between arm and maximum flow rate (12 mL/s or less versus above 12 mL/s) on 5-year IPSS
results.note: Mean 5-year IPSS with urodynamics versus routine care was 14.23 versus 12.47 at 12 mL/s or less (129 versus 126 men) and 13.03 versus 15.50 above 12 mL/s (72 versus 72). One of five prespecified subgroup variables (age, flow rate, voided volume, nocturia, storage LUTS); age showed a weak interaction (p = 0.068), voided volume, nocturia and storage LUTS showed none, and no subgroup interaction appeared for surgery rate (Table 15).

results.measure: Incremental mean cost, urodynamics minus routine care (GBP)
results.locator: HTA 2025 p33, Table 22; p32, Table 21; p35
results.note: Adjusted mean cost 4,464.41 versus 4,287.78 GBP. Increments by year: +135.86 (year 1), +167.77 (year 2), +9.21, +1.55 and -137.76 (year 5). Unit cost of a urodynamic test was 268 GBP (2020-21 NHS reference costs). Discounted at 3.5%; NHS secondary care perspective.

results.measure: Incremental mean QALYs, urodynamics minus routine care
results.note: Adjusted mean QALYs 3.490 versus 3.529; EQ-5D-5L mapped to the UK three-level value set, zero imputed after death.

results.measure: Incremental net monetary benefit at 20,000 GBP per QALY, urodynamics minus routine care (GBP)
results.note: The probability that urodynamics was cost-effective at 20,000 GBP per QALY was 21%. With a 1.5% discount rate the net monetary benefit was -983.33 (95% CI -3,446.02 to 1,479.35); with outpatient costs cut by 62% it was -1,127.15 (95% CI -3,414.44 to 1,160.14).

harms.label: Deaths by 5 years (ONS records)
harms.note: Among 415 and 386 men with routine data. Phase I deaths 11 versus 3 and Phase II deaths 17 versus 23; median time to death 35 months (interquartile range 15-50) versus 40 months (30-52). The Phase I count from ONS records differs from the 9 versus 2 reported by the trial.

delivery.label: Men with a LUTS procedure in routine data
delivery.note: 347 of 801 men in total (43.3%). Routine data contained 454 procedures (412 admitted-care, 42 outpatient): 185 of M653 endoscopic resection of prostate NEC, 96 electrotome resection, 33 laser resection, 27 (M683) and 16 (M708) listed as endoscopic insertion of a prosthesis to compress a prostatic lobe, 26 endoscopic bladder outlet incisions and 41 introductions of a therapeutic substance into the bladder (M494, a storage-LUTS treatment counted as LUTS surgery).

delivery.label: Questionnaires returned (Phase II)
delivery.note: 570 men were contactable and 550 were sent a questionnaire; the report states 416 were received, with 205 shown for routine care in Figure 3, and notes one blank questionnaire. The abstract's 205/363 (56.5%) uses the 363 men in the routine care 18-month cohort as denominator rather than the 393 randomized.

delivery.label: Urodynamics in routine data over 5 years
delivery.note: 25 further urodynamic tests appeared between 18 months and 5 years, 23 of them in routine care. Routine data identified only 265 of the 376 Phase I urodynamics cases (70%), so the report suspects poor coding of urodynamics.

delivery.label: Routine data against Phase I case report forms
delivery.value: 776/790 (98%) of Phase I findings matched: 282/291 surgical cases and 494/499 non-surgical cases.
delivery.note: 66 additional surgery cases appeared in routine data compared with Phase I, most after 18 months.

relations.note: Same question in women before stress-incontinence surgery; office evaluation alone was noninferior to adding urodynamics.
